In addition to macOS 26.6, Apple has also simultaneously released macOS Sonoma 14.8.8 and macOS Sequoia 15.7.8, which include important bug fixes. Details are as follows.

macOS Sonoma 14.8.8 and macOS Sequoia 15.7.8 are finally officially released

After as many as seven release candidate (RC) versions of testing, Apple has finally officially released macOS Sonoma 14.8.8 and macOS Sequoia 15.7.8.

The official version numbering is the same as last week's release candidate:

  • macOS Sonoma 14.8.8 (23J620)
  • macOS Sequoia 15.7.8 (24G824)

Apple's release notes only mention that these two updates provide "important security fixes" and recommend that all users still on macOS Sonoma and macOS Sequoia upgrade as soon as possible.

Over the past few weeks, Apple has released several security fixes for older versions of the system, many of which patch WebKit vulnerabilities to prevent user data from being at risk. Therefore, if you are still using macOS Sonoma or macOS Sequoia, it is recommended that you install these updates as soon as possible.

Update: Apple has announced the complete security content for macOS Sonoma 14.8.8 and macOS Sequoia 15.7.8, with the two systems combined involving more than 138 different vulnerabilities.

Are you still using macOS Sonoma or macOS Sequoia? Feel free to share in the comments section.
